definitions.explanation: A tunnel or passageway built underground for pedestrians to cross under roads, railways, or connect buildings.

examples.japanese: {地下道|ちかどう}を{通|とお}って{駅|えき}に{向|む}かう。
examples.english: I head to the station through the underground passage.

examples.japanese: この{地下道|ちかどう}は{駅|えき}とデパートを{結|むす}んでいる。
examples.english: This underground passage connects the station to the department store.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{地下道|ちかどう}を{使|つか}うと{濡|ぬ}れずに{済|す}む。
examples.english: On rainy days, using the underground passage keeps you dry.

examples.japanese: {地下道|ちかどう}には{店|みせ}が{並|なら}んでいる。
{夏|なつ}の{暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}は{地下道|ちかどう}を{通|とお}ると{涼|すず}しくて{助|たす}かる。
examples.english: On hot summer days, it's a relief to walk through the underground passage where it's cool.

notes:
COMPOSITION: {地下|ちか} (underground) + {道|どう} (road, passage)

TYPES OF UNDERGROUND PASSAGES:
・{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}{専用|せんよう}{地下道|ちかどう} - pedestrian-only underpass
・{地下街|ちかがい} - underground shopping arcade (larger, with many shops)
・{駅|えき}{地下道|ちかどう} - station underground passage

ADVANTAGES:
・{雨|あめ}に{濡|ぬ}れない - stay dry from rain
・{夏|なつ}は{涼|すず}しい - cool in summer
・{信号待|しんごうま}ちがない - no waiting at traffic lights

RELATED TERMS:
・{歩道橋|ほどうきょう} - pedestrian overpass (above-ground alternative)
・{地下鉄|ちかてつ} - subway (underground train)
・{地下街|ちかがい} - underground shopping area

NOTE: Major Japanese cities like Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya have extensive underground passage networks connecting train stations, department stores, and office buildings.
